findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent destination-calendar fallback is dead code and resolves to undefined
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (and identically in `deleteEvent` at line 315) the new fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This expression is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `find` predicate compares each calendar's externalId against a falsy value and never matches. The result is always `undefined`, whereas the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Consequence: when a booking reference has no `externalCalendarId` (e.g. bookings whose destination calendar has no externalId, or older references), Google updates are sent with `calendarId: undefined` and deletes fall through to `"primary"`, meaning updates fail and deletes can target the wrong calendar. The fallback should look up the destination calendar matching the current credential (e.g. by `credentialId`) instead of comparing against the falsy `externalCalendarId`.

findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` accesses `.integration` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which all the new fallback code paths in this PR now produce, e.g. `selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []` in confirm.handler, handleCancelBooking, webhooks, etc.), destructuring yields `undefined` and `undefined.integration` throws a TypeError, breaking booking creation for Google-Meet-located events for users without a destination calendar. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` which was null-safe. It must be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Slug condition inverted: orgs now get a slug exactly when team billing is enabled
findings.body: The change `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the original behavior while the adjacent `requestedSlug` line keeps the same condition as before. Previously the org Team record stored `slug` when billing was disabled and `requestedSlug` when billing was enabled; now `slug` is set when billing is enabled and nothing is set when it is disabled. This is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and will break organization subdomain creation on instances where `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false (no slug persisted) and double-set slug/requestedSlug when it is true.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first calendar reference, leaving stale events on other hosts' calendars
findings.body: `updateAllCalendarEvents` was extended to loop over all `_calendar` references (to support multiple destination calendars for collective events), but the merge branch that deletes the old booking's calendar events still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`, deleting only the first calendar reference. For a collective booking with events on two hosts' calendars, rescheduling to a new booking leaves the old event on the second host's calendar. The deletion should iterate all old `_calendar` references (using each reference's `credentialId`/`externalCalendarId`).

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, and afterwards `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`. So for a collective event whose organizer has no destination calendar but whose co-hosts do, all team destination calendars are discarded and no calendar events are created on any host's calendar (EventManager falls back to the organizer's first connected credential). The fallback should be `[]` (matching every other call site in this PR) or the team calendars should be assigned as the initial value.

findings.title: CalDAV BaseCalendarService ignores per-credential destination calendars, breaking multi-host collective events
findings.body: `createEvent` filters the calendar list using only the first destination calendar's externalId (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`). The `Calendar` interface was changed in this PR to pass `credentialId` to `createEvent` specifically so services can pick the destination matching the credential being used (as the Google service now does), but the CalDAV base class was not updated: its `createEvent(event)` signature doesn't accept `credentialId`, and when `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` invokes it once per host destination, every invocation still targets the first host's calendar. For a collective event with two CalDAV hosts, the second host's credentials are used to write into the first host's calendar URL (failing or creating the event in the wrong place) and the second host's calendar never receives the event. The same single-first-destination pattern also remains in the office365 and lark services, so multi-destination support effectively only works for Google Calendar.

findings.title: Cancel-all-recurring branch deletes only the first calendar reference per booking using the organizer's credentials
findings.body: In the `recurringEvent && allRemainingBookings` path, deletion iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's credentials only) and, for each updated booking, deletes only `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` — the first calendar reference. With the new multi-reference support this PR introduces for collective events, co-hosts' calendar events are never deleted when cancelling all remaining recurring bookings, and the outer loop over `bookingCalendarReference` re-runs the same deletion for every reference, duplicating work. Deletion should use each reference's own `credentialId` and iterate all `_calendar` references per updated booking.

findings.title: No automated tests cover the new multi-destination-calendar behavior, and payload expectations are inconsistent
findings.body: The PR checklist states no tests were added, yet it changes a core type (`CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar`) consumed by every booking flow. The only test change is updating one expected webhook payload from `destinationCalendar: null` to `[]` (BOOKING_REJECTED) while BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect `null` — reflecting inconsistent fallbacks (`handleNewBooking` uses `null`, `confirm.handler` uses `[]`). There is no test exercising a collective event with multiple hosts each having a calendar app (create/reschedule/cancel across two destination calendars), which is exactly the scenario the PR claims to fix; regressions like the Google update/delete fallback bug and the empty-array crash in EventManager.create would not be caught.
